title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-olivia
content:
Personal scratchpad / incident breadcrumbs: streaming SSE chunking + backpressure repro

Date: 2025-02-18 -> updated 2025-02-21
Owner: Olivia Chen
Context: intermittent client-side parse failures and server memory growth observed for streaming text/event-stream responses. Issue appears when long-running sessions + high-concurrency (Dedicated env) cause partial JSON chunks and occasional client JSON.parse errors.

Summary of symptoms:
- Clients (node fetch / browser EventSource wrapper / Python requests) sometimes receive partial JSON frames (truncated) that lead to "Unexpected end of JSON input" or "SyntaxError: Unexpected token \"\"\"" when trying to parse assembled chunks.
- Server-side: long tail of requests shows growing write buffers in the runtime (observed in jemalloc stats + p99 write queue length).
- Repro is easier with HTTP proxy (nginx) in front of runtime; disabling proxy buffering reduces occurrences.
- Problem more frequent over HTTP/2 in our load tests.

Environment tested:
- Local: go-serving-runtime v2.3.1 (dev build) on linux (Ubuntu 22.04), node 20.9, python 3.11
- Staging: serving-runtime service behind nginx (1.22) / envoy in k8s, HTTP/2 enabled, GKE nodepools (n1-standard-4)

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Start a simple streaming endpoint locally (we used the runtime dev server). Then run clients below.

2) curl repro (sse)\- use -N/--no-buffer so curl writes as data arrives:

curl -sN -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" \n  -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/streaming-complete \n  -d '{"input":"tokenized prompt to stream partial JSON objects with delays"}'

Expected: series of lines like "event: message\n data: {\"chunk\":\"...\"}\n\n"
Observed (intermittent): data lines where JSON payload is split across network frames and client gets partial data then EOF: e.g.

...data: {"chunk":"this is a partial
<connection close>


client tries JSON.parse on single data chunk -> throws Unexpected end of JSON input

3) node fetch reader (repro script)
// node-streaming-repro.js
const res = await fetch('http://localhost:8080/v1/streaming-complete', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'long prompt with deliberate pauses' }) });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
let buf = '';
while(true){
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  buf += new TextDecoder().decode(value, { stream: true });
  // naive split on newlines produced by server
  const parts = buf.split('\n\n');
  for(let i=0;i<parts.length-1;i++){
    const p = parts[i].replace(/^data: /,'');
    try{ JSON.parse(p); } catch(e){ console.error('PARSE FAIL', e.message, p.slice(0,120)); }
  }
  buf = parts[parts.length-1];
}

Observed: PARSE FAIL intermittently. Value fragments often look like valid JSON trimmed in the middle of a unicode sequence (rare) or split at a token boundary.

4) python requests streaming client (repro):
import requests
with requests.post('http://localhost:8080/v1/streaming-complete', json={'input':'...'}, stream=True) as r:
    for line in r.iter_lines(chunk_size=64):
        if line:
            s = line.decode('utf-8')
            if s.startswith('data: '):
                try:
                    json.loads(s[6:])
                except Exception as e:
                    print('FAIL', e, s[:120])

Observation: more likely to fail when chunk_size small and when nginx buffering on.

Commands tried (to isolate):
- curl with/without -N; --no-buffer reduces but does not eliminate errors.
- Disabled nginx proxy_buffering (proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on) -> drop in error rate in staging.
- Force HTTP/1.1 (curl --http1.1) -> fewer errors than http2 in same load scenario.
- Added explicit flush in runtime after writing each SSE event (runtime write + flush) -> error rate decreased but still present under concurrency.
- Introduced small delay between writes (10ms) -> mitigates but not acceptable as permanent fix.

Server logs / error snippets:
- client errors: "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input"
- runtime logs: "write buffer backlog increasing: write_queue=384 -> p99_write_latency=120ms"
- nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream" (rare)
- node client: ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR when multiplexed with other streams

Hypotheses:
1) Multi-layer buffering: nginx (or other proxy) + HTTP/2 frame coalescing + Node/python reader chunk boundaries cause event payloads to be split unpredictably. Some clients assume each SSE data event is atomic and parse JSON immediately; if server produces large JSON that gets split across TCP frames, the client parse attempt on partial data will fail.
2) Backpressure handling in runtime: when client is slow to consume, the runtime's send buffer grows; we may be coalescing multiple events into a single network write and then the proxy splits them at an inconvenient boundary. If server flush semantics are not strict (missing flush() or using stdio buffering), event boundaries aren't guaranteed.
3) HTTP/2 specific behavior: HTTP/2 HEADERS+DATA frames and multiplexing can interact with our SSE heuristic code (written for chunked transfer) and cause unexpected partial frames when using HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 proxies.
4) Incorrect Content-Type / line endings (CRLF vs LF) can cause some clients to treat lines differently; consistent line endings are important.

Short-term mitigations (applied to staging):
- Set nginx: proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; add proxy_set_header Connection "" to avoid connection upgrade oddities.
- Add server-side sanity checks: if data chunk does not parse as JSON, buffer it (up to X bytes) and wait for next chunk instead of failing immediately. This is defensive at the client wrapper level.
- Instrumentation: per-stream queued_bytes metric, number of flush calls, time since last flush, number of requeued events. Added counters in runtime: sse_flush_count, sse_buffered_bytes.

Long-term fixes under consideration:
- Make SSE generation emit explicit event boundaries that are always small (split JSON into smaller chunks carrying sequence numbers and a final marker) so clients can reassemble deterministically. Con: more overhead / more events.
- Ensure the runtime disables Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) on streaming sockets to reduce coalescing latency.
- Add an HTTP/2-aware SSE implementation path (forcing the runtime to use DATA frames with end_stream=false in a way that preserves logical events).
- Improve proxy defaults in k8s manifests to disable buffering for streaming endpoints (ingress annotation docs).
- Client SDK: provide a robust SSE parser that accumulates partial data and only attempts JSON.parse on complete event payloads (recommended for SDKs).

Small repro harness included (in repo): tests/streaming/sse_chunking_repro.py and node tests. Quick run:
- Start runtime: make dev-run
- Run load: for i in {1..50}; do node node-streaming-repro.js & done  # to produce concurrency
- Observe parse fails in stdout.

Next actions assigned:
- Evan: add sse_buffered_bytes metric + dashboard panel (due 2025-02-24)
- Kyla: add nginx ingress annotation to disable proxy buffering for streaming endpoints and run A/B (due 2025-02-23)
- Olivia: prototype HTTP/2-safe SSE path and add TCP_NODELAY toggle (WIP)

Notes / context snippets:
"If you attempt to JSON.parse every data: field as it arrives you will hit partial-parsing issues. Always accumulate until you see the blank line that delimits the event and then parse." -- internal reminder

Loose TODOs:
- Add more robust unit tests that simulate proxy frame splits (http2 and http1.1)
- Evaluate whether the runtime should set Content-Length=unknown and rely on chunked transfer rather than streaming heuristics
- Look into migration to event-stream framing with length-prefixed messages (binary) for SDKs that need reliability over text-based SSE.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above.

Appendix: small failing example captured from node reader (raw bytes hex around boundary):
... 7b 22 63 68 75 6e 6b 22 3a 22 74 68 69 73 20 69 73 20 61 20 70 61 72 74 69 61 6c 22 7d 0a 0a 5b 5d ...

If you need this reproduced live I can run it against staging with test token (opens up staging logs).

-- Olivia
